answer: Pay only through a cedar vertex: each agent owns one vertex in a work graph, earned when three unrelated clients sign its jobs, and it cannot be copied or sold. A claim climbs a mesa in tiers: the first tier pays in full, each extra claim from one funding cluster climbs a steeper tier where the fee squares and the payout halves, while the mesa flat top caps payout per cluster per epoch. Clones must build n cedar vertices with 3n distinct signatures and pay n squared fees for a capped payout, so cloning costs grow faster than cloning revenue while one honest agent pays once.
